---
title: "Beyond the NHL: international hockey and other eras"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
# This article calls the NHL's and the IIHF's APIs. It runs when the docs
# site is built (BLUELINER_LIVE=true) and is shown without output otherwise.
live <- identical(Sys.getenv("BLUELINER_LIVE"), "true")
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = live, fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 4, dpi = 110)
options(tibble.print_min = 6, width = 95)
```

The NHL's APIs reach past its own regular season and playoffs: the
best-on-best tournaments its players have played in since 1976, the tracking
of the 4 Nations Face-Off, and every season back to 1917-18. The IIHF's live
feed adds a shot map of every game it runs. This article goes through each.

```{r}
library(bluelineR)
```

## Every best-on-best tournament

The NHL keeps the record of every tournament its players have played in:
five Canada Cups, three World Cups of Hockey, the Olympics from 1998 to 2014
and in 2026, and the 4 Nations Face-Off. `nhl_international_winners()` is
the game that decided each:

```{r}
winners <- nhl_international_winners()
winners[, c("tournament", "year", "winning_tricode", "winning_score", "losing_tricode", "losing_score", "overtime")]
```

Each player's and club's numbers at each tournament are in
`nhl_international()`; here are the 2026 Olympics' scoring leaders:

```{r}
oly <- nhl_international("skater", "olympics", 2026)
oly[, c("first_name", "last_name", "tri_code", "games_played", "goals", "assists", "points")]
```

and the Olympic careers, with medals:

```{r}
careers <- nhl_international_careers("skater", olympics = TRUE)
careers[, c("first_name", "last_name", "team_name", "tournaments_played", "games_played", "points", "gold_medals", "total_medals")]
```

## The 4 Nations final, from the tracking

The 4 Nations Face-Off was played on NHL ice with the NHL's tracking, so
its goals have the same frames as any NHL goal: every skater and the puck,
ten times a second. Connor McDavid's overtime winner in the final:

```{r goal, fig.height = 4.6, fig.alt = "Connor McDavid's overtime winner in the 4 Nations final: every player's position as the puck goes in, with the last two seconds of each path."}
frames <- nhl_goal_tracking(2024200007, 1443)
plot_goal(frames, title = "Connor McDavid, overtime winner, 4 Nations final, 20 Feb 2025")
```

`animate_goal()` plays it back, with the clubs' logos and the tournament's
at centre ice:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
four_nations <- paste0("https://assets.nhle.com/special_event_season/20242025/svg/",
                       "4n-2025-championship-extwm-en_light.svg")
animate_goal(frames, "mcdavid-4-nations.mp4", goal = nhl_goal_replay(2024200007, 1443),
             logos = TRUE, centre_logo = four_nations)
```

<img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethanrawson/bluelineR/Model/man/figures/README-hero.gif" alt="Connor McDavid's overtime winner in the 4 Nations final, played back from the tracking." width="100%" />

## The Olympic final, shot by shot

The Olympics are not on NHL tracking, but the IIHF's live feed places every
shot on the ice. The 2026 men's final, won by Jack Hughes in overtime:

```{r}
shots <- iihf_shots(1010000058)
table(shots$team, shots$result)
shots[shots$result == "goal", c("period", "time", "team", "player_name", "distance")]
```

```{r shots, fig.height = 4.6, fig.alt = "Shot map of the 2026 Olympic men's final, Canada against the United States, each club at its own end."}
plot_shots(shots)
```

The same functions cover the IIHF's World Championships, World Juniors and
women's and under-18 tournaments from 2019 on: `iihf_schedule()` lists a
tournament's games.

## Other eras

A 1950s season and a 2020s one were played in different leagues: fewer
games, fewer skaters dressed, and more or fewer goals a night.
`nhl_era_adjust()` rescales each season to one scoring environment (by
default the last ten completed seasons over 82 games), so the best seasons
of four eras read on one scale:

```{r}
best_season <- function(id) {
  p <- nhl_player(id)
  s <- p$season_totals
  s <- s[s$league_abbrev == "NHL" & s$game_type_id == 2, ]
  out <- s[which.max(s$points), c("season", "goals", "assists", "points")]
  out$player <- paste(p$bio$first_name, p$bio$last_name)
  out
}
best <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(8448000, 8447400, 8448782, 8478402), best_season))
nhl_era_adjust(best)[, c("player", "season", "goals", "assists", "points", "adj_goals", "adj_assists", "adj_points")]
```

`nhl_league_env()` is the table behind it: every season since 1917-18, with
its games, goals and assists a game and roster size. `nhl_stat_eras()` says
what the NHL kept in each era, from goals and assists in 1917-18 to the
tracking of today.
